.github/workflows/companions.yaml.text:
name: Companions

# Keeps the companion images core embeds present in the registry. core pins
# each companion tag (codeflydev/<name>:<version>) via info.codefly.yaml and
# agents pull those exact tags at runtime, so a pinned-but-unpushed tag
# breaks every Codefly-native build at the companion pull.
#
# Two jobs:
#   publish - an explicit operator action that builds+pushes the whole set,
#             then verifies it. This requires Docker Hub release credentials.
#   verify  - a standing gate (CLI release + daily) that fails fast when an
#             embedded public tag is missing, without mutating the registry.
#
# The fail-fast-on-bump gate ideally also lives in core's CI (that is where
# companion versions change); this repo runs it against core@main on a
# schedule so a regression surfaces here too.

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Daily, so an embedded tag that goes missing is caught within a day.
    - cron: '0 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      core_ref:
        description: 'core ref (tag/branch/sha) to publish/verify companions from'
        required: false
        default: 'main'

# Publishing mutates immutable tags. Two overlapping runs would interleave those
# pushes, leaving each tag naming whichever run finished last while both report
# success. Queue instead of cancelling: a cancelled run would leave the fleet
# half-published.
concurrency:
  group: companions-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish:
    name: Publish and verify companion images
    # Companion versions are owned by core, not by the CLI version. Publishing
    # is therefore an explicit registry mutation, never a side effect of every
    # unrelated CLI release.
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # 360 minutes is the GitHub-hosted ceiling, not a tunable: no value here
    # can buy this job more time. It is set explicitly because the whole set is
    # built serially and the proto image compiles ~10 Go plugins with its arm64
    # half under QEMU, so the run is within sight of the cap. If it starts
    # timing out, the fix is to fan the companions out across jobs — the base
    # first, then its dependents, which is now possible because a dependent
    # resolves its base from the registry through CODEFLY_BASE_IMAGE rather
    # than from a locally-built image.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    outputs:
      companions: ${{ steps.published.outputs.companions }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out cli
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5
        with:
          path: cli

      - name: Check out core
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5
        with:
          repository: codefly-dev/core
          ref: ${{ github.event.inputs.core_ref || 'main' }}
          token: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          # buildLinuxCLI expects core/ and cli/ as siblings: language
          # companions COPY --from a linux binary cross-compiled from ../cli.
          path: core

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16 # v6
        with:
          go-version-file: cli/go.mod
          cache: false

      - name: Build the codefly CLI
        working-directory: cli
        run: GOWORK=off GOBIN="${{ github.workspace }}/bin" go install ./cmd/codefly

      # A multi-platform buildx push builds every image as one manifest, so the
      # arm64 stages need an emulator (QEMU) and a builder that can emit a
      # manifest list.
      - name: Set up QEMU
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@c7c53464625b32c7a7e944ae62b3e17d2b600130 # v3

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@8d2750c68a42422c14e847fe6c8ac0403b4cbd6f # v3

      # Companion tags resolve through resources.ImageRegistry, which is
      # ghcr.io/codefly-dev — authenticating anywhere else leaves every push
      # unauthenticated and the whole run publishes nothing.
      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@c94ce9fb468520275223c153574b00df6fe4bcc9 # v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Publish every companion at its pinned version
        # Publish multi-arch: every language service agent ships linux/arm64, so
        # a companion must too or it can't run a single language service on an
        # arm64 host. One manifest list serves both arches.
        #
        # --force-docker: proto ships a flake.nix and the nix path cannot emit a
        # multi-platform manifest, so a runner with nix installed would abort
        # the run on proto after the earlier companions were already pushed.
        # --pull: refreshes the floating upstream bases the Dockerfiles sit on
        # (golang:1.27-alpine, node:...-alpine) so a rebuild picks up their
        # latest patch instead of a cached older layer. It has nothing to do
        # with the codefly base companion: that one is resolved by reference
        # and passed as CODEFLY_BASE_IMAGE, not inherited from the cache.
        # --published-manifest: records what this run actually pushed, which is
        # the only set that may be attested below.
        run: >-
          ${{ github.workspace }}/bin/codefly companion publish --all
          --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          --force-docker
          --pull
          --core-dir "${{ github.workspace }}/core"
          --published-manifest "${{ runner.temp }}/published.json"

      # Written whether or not publish succeeded, so a partial run still
      # attests the companions it did push. `if: always()` covers the publish
      # step failing; the file is absent only if publish never ran at all.
      - name: Collect what this run published
        id: published
        if: always()
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          file="${{ runner.temp }}/published.json"
          # Absent means publish never reached the build: report an empty set
          # rather than failing here and masking the real failure above. A file
          # that exists but does not parse is a different matter and must fail.
          if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
            echo "companions=[]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "companions=$(jq -c . "$file")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Verify every embedded tag is in the registry
        run: ${{ github.workspace }}/bin/codefly companion verify --core-dir "${{ github.workspace }}/core"

  # Provenance is attested per image because actions/attest-build-provenance
  # signs one subject at a time.
  #
  # The matrix is what the publish run reported pushing, never the full set
  # core declares. A build-provenance attestation asserts that this workflow
  # run produced these bits, so attesting a tag the run skipped as already
  # published would sign a claim that is simply false — and it is pushed to
  # the registry and a public transparency log, where it cannot be withdrawn.
  attest:
    name: Attest published companion images
    needs: publish
    # An empty matrix produces no jobs, which is the correct outcome when a run
    # published nothing. The guard is for the publish job failing outright.
    if: needs.publish.outputs.companions != '' && needs.publish.outputs.companions != '[]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # write, not read: push-to-registry uploads the attestation to ghcr as an
      # OCI artifact, which read cannot do — it 403s after publish has already
      # mutated the registry.
      packages: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.publish.outputs.companions) }}
    steps:
      - uses: docker/login-action@c94ce9fb468520275223c153574b00df6fe4bcc9 # v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # The digest comes from the publish run's own report of what it pushed,
      # not from resolving the tag here. A tag is mutable and this job runs after
      # the whole publish job has finished, so re-reading it could attest an
      # image this workflow run never built — a claim that is then pushed to a
      # public transparency log, where it cannot be withdrawn.
      - name: Check the publish run reported a digest
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${{ matrix.digest }}" ]; then
            echo "publish reported no digest for ${{ matrix.image }}; refusing to attest an image this run cannot name exactly" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@e8998f949152b193b063cb0ec769d69d929409be # v2
        with:
          subject-name: ghcr.io/codefly-dev/${{ matrix.companion }}
          subject-digest: ${{ matrix.digest }}
          push-to-registry: true

  verify:
    name: Verify embedded companion tags
    # Standing read-only gate. A manual run uses the publish job above, whose
    # final step verifies the same immutable tags after pushing.
    if: github.event_name == 'release' || github.event_name == 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out cli
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5
        with:
          path: cli

      - name: Check out core
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5
        with:
          repository: codefly-dev/core
          ref: ${{ github.event.inputs.core_ref || 'main' }}
          token: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          path: core

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16 # v6
        with:
          go-version-file: cli/go.mod
          cache: false

      - name: Build the codefly CLI
        working-directory: cli
        run: GOWORK=off GOBIN="${{ github.workspace }}/bin" go install ./cmd/codefly

      - name: Verify a linux/arm64 companion can resolve every language agent
        # Guards the arm64 companion footgun: publishing an arm64 companion is
        # only safe while every language agent still ships a linux/arm64 asset.
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: ${{ github.workspace }}/bin/codefly agent verify-platform linux/arm64

      - name: Verify every embedded tag is in the registry
        run: ${{ github.workspace }}/bin/codefly companion verify --core-dir "${{ github.workspace }}/core"

.github/workflows/go.yml.text:
name: Go CLI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  quality:
    name: ${{ matrix.gate }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # The race and coverage gates take 4-5 minutes on a warm cache with ±40s of
    # runner variance, so a 5-minute budget cancels borderline-healthy runs.
    # 8 minutes keeps a hang from burning a full runner-hour while leaving the
    # suite real headroom.
    timeout-minutes: 8
    # `conformance_rows` is the set of docs/supported-matrix.md rows this gate
    # claims to prove. A claimed row's tests can no longer skip themselves when
    # the backend is missing, and the always-run receipt check below fails if a
    # claimed row never ran.
    env:
      CODEFLY_CONFORMANCE_REQUIRED: ${{ matrix.conformance_rows }}
      CODEFLY_CONFORMANCE_RECEIPTS: ${{ github.workspace }}/conformance-receipts
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        include:
          - gate: bootstrap-audit
          - gate: control-integration
            conformance_rows: linux-amd64-nix-run
          - gate: coverage
            conformance_rows: linux-amd64-source,linux-amd64-native-npm
          - gate: race
            conformance_rows: linux-amd64-source,linux-amd64-native-npm
    steps:
      - name: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5

      - name: Set up Go
        if: matrix.gate == 'coverage' || matrix.gate == 'race'
        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16 # v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: false

      # The production source-workspace regression runs the released Python
      # plugin on a fresh Linux host. Provision its declared uv runtime in the
      # ordinary test lanes so the proof exercises real tests instead of an
      # environment-blocked agent response.
      - name: Set up uv
        if: matrix.gate == 'coverage' || matrix.gate == 'race'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c771a70e6277c0a99b617c7a806ffedaca235ff9 # v9.0.0

      # pkg/librarystore's npm backend shells out to the real npm CLI (npm pack,
      # npm publish) against an httptest registry rather than mocking the store;
      # those tests need node/npm on the runner.
      - name: Set up Node
        if: matrix.gate == 'coverage' || matrix.gate == 'race'
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7

      # Restore before the bootstrap action: that action compiles the CLI, so
      # restoring afterward would make its cache permanently ineffective.
      # Cache only compiled artifacts. Caching GOMODCACHE alongside a Go
      # toolchain directive can race setup-go's toolchain install and produce
      # tar restore conflicts.
      - name: Restore Go build cache
        uses: actions/cache@caa296126883cff596d87d8935842f9db880ef25 # v5
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/go-build
          key: cli-go-build-v3-${{ matrix.gate }}-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
          restore-keys: |
            cli-go-build-v3-${{ matrix.gate }}-${{ runner.os }}-

      # This is both the canonical bootstrap and the cross-repository action
      # contract consumed by Codefly products. Dogfood the local action so a
      # release cannot publish an installer that CI never exercised.
      - name: install Codefly
        if: matrix.gate == 'bootstrap-audit' || matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        uses: ./.github/actions/install

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: go mod download

      - name: Verify the composed-module command is packaged
        if: matrix.gate == 'bootstrap-audit'
        run: codefly sync module --help

      # govulncheck gate via the CLI (replaces scripts/govulncheck.sh):
      # suppressions + staleness from .govulncheck.yaml, fails only on
      # actionable (upstream-fixed) findings.
      - name: govulncheck audit
        if: matrix.gate == 'bootstrap-audit'
        run: |
          go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest
          codefly audit go --dir .

      - name: Test with coverage
        if: matrix.gate == 'coverage'
        run: go test -failfast ./... -coverprofile=cover.out -covermode=atomic -coverpkg=./...

      - name: Check test coverage
        if: matrix.gate == 'coverage'
        id: coverage
        uses: vladopajic/go-test-coverage@f94bcf0d6b9fa5fb8b783830b22648f6c17475e2 # v2
        with:
          config: ./.testcoverage.yaml

      # The CGO-free companion/self-cross build (`-tags codefly_nosemantic`,
      # CGO_ENABLED=0) selects pkg/engine/source_nosemantic.go. `codefly
      # companion publish` exercises it only in companions.yaml, which needs
      # Docker; verify here, unconditionally, that the variant both links
      # statically and runs its base source behavior. Without this a regression
      # in the analyzer-free variant would surface only at publish time.
      - name: Verify CGO-free (companion) build variant
        if: matrix.gate == 'coverage'
        env:
          CGO_ENABLED: "0"
        run: |
          go build -tags codefly_nosemantic -ldflags '-s -w -extldflags "-static"' -o /dev/null .
          go test -tags codefly_nosemantic ./pkg/engine/ -run '^TestNewSourceExecutesLanguageNeutralOperation$' -count=1

      - name: Test with race detection
        if: matrix.gate == 'race'
        run: go test -failfast -race ./... -v

      # The cross-process control-ownership proof drives the CLI built by the
      # install action above as a real subprocess against real sockets. It runs
      # here rather than in the default lanes because those would have to link
      # a CLI binary of their own; it needs neither Nix nor an agent, so it runs
      # before both and fails fast.
      - name: Run the cross-process control-ownership proof
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        run: go test -tags=integration -run '^TestRunRefusesAControlAddressAnotherProcessOwns$|^TestConcurrentDisposableRunsClaimDistinctIdentities$' ./cmd/run -v

      # The pinned Redis agent resolves a Nix runtime during runtime-init, so the
      # proof needs Nix on the runner or the agent fails with "nix is not
      # installed" instead of exercising the real dependency. Mirrors core's CI.
      - name: Install Nix
        # Strict — nix is core to the platform; if it doesn't install,
        # CI must fail loud rather than silently skipping nix tests.
        # DeterminateSystems' installer is the de-facto standard for
        # GH Actions: deterministic, no daemon issues on ephemeral runners.
        #
        # This used to follow @main. It is now pinned to a release, like every
        # other action here, so the comment records the tag at the pinned commit
        # (v23) rather than the branch it was reached through — Dependabot
        # resolves the version from the tag at the SHA, so a `# main` comment
        # would be silently rewritten to a version on the first bump.
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        uses: DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@3138316df39ed29be04236d7ffc686fa525866aa # v23

      - name: Allow unprivileged user namespaces (for bwrap)
        # Ubuntu 24.04 ships with kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1
        # which blocks bubblewrap's user-namespace setup ("bwrap: setting up uid
        # map: Permission denied"). Disabling the restriction is the standard CI
        # workaround — bwrap then works in unprivileged mode, which is what the
        # nix runtime's sandbox expects.
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        run: sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0

      - name: Install the pinned Redis agent
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        run: codefly agent install codefly.dev/redis:0.0.74

      - name: Run the in-process run-profile proof
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        run: go test -tags=integration -run '^TestRunProfilesStartRealDependencyShapesInProcess$' ./pkg/control -v

      # Pull separately from the proof below so a cold-cache image fetch is
      # attributed to its own step instead of inflating the test's wall time —
      # this gate shares one 8-minute job budget with the Nix install above.
      # Keep the tag in step with teardownPostgresImage in
      # pkg/orchestration/teardown_postgres_integration_test.go.
      - name: Pull the ordered-teardown proof's database image
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        run: docker pull postgres:16-alpine

      # Ordered teardown (F09): the consumer holds its drain open and commits a
      # final transaction to a disposable Postgres; the database must not begin
      # stopping until that commit returned. Needs Docker, which the runner has.
      # It claims no conformance row: the ordering contract is backend-neutral,
      # so it proves nothing about a docs/supported-matrix.md row.
      - name: Run the ordered-teardown acceptance proof
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        run: go test -tags=integration -run '^TestFlowStopHoldsPostgresUntilItsConsumerCommits$' ./pkg/orchestration -v

      # Always-run so a failed or filtered-out test still has to account for
      # the rows its job claimed. Keep these last: they audit every step above.
      - name: Verify conformance receipts
        if: always() && matrix.conformance_rows != ''
        run: ./scripts/verify-conformance-receipts.sh

      - name: Upload conformance receipts
        if: always() && matrix.conformance_rows != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: conformance-receipts-${{ matrix.gate }}
          path: conformance-receipts/
          if-no-files-found: warn

  # golangci-lint runs as its own job, not a quality gate, for two reasons:
  # only-new-issues has a well-defined baseline only against a pull-request base
  # branch (on push there is no diff to gate against), and a cold-cache
  # whole-repository analysis needs more headroom than the 5-minute quality
  # budget. Pinned to match the version documented in the Makefile (`make
  # lint`). only-new-issues gates the PR on newly introduced findings so the
  # pre-existing backlog does not block work while the standard is enforced.
  lint:
    name: lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16 # v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: false

      - name: golangci-lint
        uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@4afd733a84b1f43292c63897423277bb7f4313a9 # v8
        with:
          # v2.13.1 bundles staticcheck (honnef.co/go/tools) v0.8.0, the first
          # release that understands Go 1.27 stdlib source; v2.12.2's v0.7.0
          # panics in its IR builder analyzing 1.27 packages. Keep in sync with
          # GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION in the Makefile.
          version: v2.13.1
          # Build the linter from source under the module's Go toolchain
          # (1.27) instead of downloading the prebuilt binary, which is built
          # with an older Go and refuses to lint a module targeting a newer
          # one ("the Go language version used to build golangci-lint is lower
          # than the targeted Go version"). Matches `make lint`.
          install-mode: goinstall
          only-new-issues: true

  # pkg/web/go-grpc/out is a committed, generated artifact: web/dashboard builds
  # into it and go:embed ships it inside the CLI binary (see the Makefile's
  # `dashboard` target, which is the only other place it is produced).
  #
  # Nothing else in CI runs npm, so without this job a dependency bump under
  # web/dashboard changes package.json and package-lock.json, leaves out/
  # untouched, and passes every Go gate — TestHandlerServesDashboard included,
  # because that test asserts against the committed bundle and so cannot notice
  # that the bundle no longer corresponds to the declared dependencies. The
  # binary would ship a dashboard built from the old dependency tree while the
  # lockfile claimed the new one, and the drift would surface at the next manual
  # `make dashboard`, several merges downstream of the bump that caused it.
  #
  # The build is byte-reproducible from the lockfile, so a clean tree is a fair
  # gate rather than a flaky one.
  dashboard:
    name: dashboard
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5

      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7
        with:
          # Pinned rather than left to the runner default: this job's whole
          # value is that a dirty out/ means the dependencies moved, so the
          # toolchain producing out/ must not drift underneath it.
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: web/dashboard/package-lock.json

      # npm ci, not npm install: it fails closed on a package.json that has
      # drifted from the lockfile instead of silently resolving something else.
      - name: Rebuild the embedded dashboard
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd web/dashboard
          npm ci
          npm run build

      # --intent-to-add so a newly emitted asset (an untracked file) is visible
      # to `git diff`; without it the check would only catch modifications and
      # deletions, and a build that added a chunk would pass while out/ was
      # missing it.
      - name: Fail if the committed bundle is stale
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git add --intent-to-add -- pkg/web/go-grpc/out
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- pkg/web/go-grpc/out; then
            echo "::error::pkg/web/go-grpc/out does not match a build of web/dashboard. Run 'make dashboard' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

.github/workflows/release.yaml.text:
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*.*.*"

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  id-token: write
  attestations: write
  artifact-metadata: write

jobs:
  release:
    name: Qualify and publish
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - name: Check out the tagged source
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16 # v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: false

      - name: Install Syft
        id: syft
        uses: anchore/sbom-action/download-syft@e22c389904149dbc22b58101806040fa8d37a610 # v0
        with:
          syft-version: v1.44.0

      - name: Load and verify the release signing key
        env:
          CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/codefly-release-signing-key.pem
          RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          umask 077
          printf '%s' "$RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH"
          openssl pkey -in "$CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH" -check -noout
          key_fingerprint="$(
            openssl pkey -in "$CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH" -pubout -outform DER |
              sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1
          )"
          certificate_fingerprint="$(
            openssl x509 -in pkg/cliupdate/release-signing-cert.pem -pubkey -noout |
              openssl pkey -pubin -outform DER |
              sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1
          )"
          test "$key_fingerprint" = "$certificate_fingerprint"

      - name: Qualify the clean tag
        env:
          CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/codefly-release-signing-key.pem
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          SYFT_PATH: ${{ steps.syft.outputs.cmd }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          manifest_version="$(sed -n 's/^version:[[:space:]]*//p' pkg/cli/info.yaml)"
          test "$RELEASE_TAG" = "v$manifest_version"
          test "$(git rev-list -n 1 "$RELEASE_TAG")" = "$GITHUB_SHA"
          git diff --exit-code
          # The released Gateway imports Core's tree-sitter-backed project
          # inspection. Build inside the maintained cross image so the clean
          # tag is qualified with CGO and real compilers for every target.
          docker run --rm \
            -e CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH \
            -e RELEASE_TAG \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE:/workspace" \
            -v "$RUNNER_TEMP:$RUNNER_TEMP" \
            -v "$SYFT_PATH:/usr/local/bin/syft:ro" \
            -w /workspace \
            ghcr.io/goreleaser/goreleaser-cross:v1.26.4 \
            check
          docker run --rm \
            -e CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH \
            -e RELEASE_TAG \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE:/workspace" \
            -v "$RUNNER_TEMP:$RUNNER_TEMP" \
            -v "$SYFT_PATH:/usr/local/bin/syft:ro" \
            -w /workspace \
            ghcr.io/goreleaser/goreleaser-cross:v1.26.4 \
            release --snapshot --clean

          for target in darwin:amd64 darwin:arm64 linux:amd64 linux:arm64; do
            goos="${target%%:*}"
            goarch="${target##*:}"
            jq -e --arg goos "$goos" --arg goarch "$goarch" \
              '[.[] | select(.type == "Archive" and .goos == $goos and .goarch == $goarch)] | length == 1' \
              dist/artifacts.json
          done
          jq -e '[.[] | select(.type == "SBOM")] | length == 4' dist/artifacts.json
          jq -e '[.[] | select(.type == "Signature")] | length == 1' dist/artifacts.json
          test -s dist/checksums.txt
          test -s dist/checksums.txt.sig

          openssl x509 -in pkg/cliupdate/release-signing-cert.pem -pubkey -noout > "$RUNNER_TEMP/codefly-release-public-key.pem"
          openssl dgst -sha256 \
            -verify "$RUNNER_TEMP/codefly-release-public-key.pem" \
            -signature dist/checksums.txt.sig \
            dist/checksums.txt
          (cd dist && sha256sum --check checksums.txt)

      - name: Publish the immutable release and Homebrew cask
        env:
          CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/codefly-release-signing-key.pem
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          HOMEBREW_TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          MACOS_SIGN_P12: ${{ secrets.CODEFLY_MACOS_SIGN_P12 }}
          MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CODEFLY_MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD }}
          MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.CODEFLY_MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID }}
          MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.CODEFLY_MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID }}
          MACOS_NOTARY_KEY: ${{ secrets.CODEFLY_MACOS_NOTARY_KEY }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          SYFT_PATH: ${{ steps.syft.outputs.cmd }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          test "$(gh api "repos/codefly-dev/cli/commits/$RELEASE_TAG" --jq .sha)" = "$GITHUB_SHA"
          docker run --rm \
            -e CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH \
            -e GITHUB_TOKEN \
            -e GH_TOKEN \
            -e HOMEBREW_TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN \
            -e MACOS_SIGN_P12 \
            -e MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD \
            -e MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID \
            -e MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID \
            -e MACOS_NOTARY_KEY \
            -e RELEASE_TAG \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE:/workspace" \
            -v "$RUNNER_TEMP:$RUNNER_TEMP" \
            -v "$SYFT_PATH:/usr/local/bin/syft:ro" \
            -w /workspace \
            ghcr.io/goreleaser/goreleaser-cross:v1.26.4 \
            release --clean

  attest:
    name: Attest published artifacts
    needs: release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
      artifact-metadata: write
    steps:
      - name: Download published artifacts
        env:
          # The repository-scoped workflow token is the read authority for this
          # job. GH_PAT is needed only by publication because it also updates the
          # separate Homebrew repository; carrying it into verification made a
          # successfully published release appear absent to `gh release`.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets"
          gh release download "$RELEASE_TAG" \
            --repo codefly-dev/cli \
            --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets" \
            --pattern "codefly_*.tar.gz" \
            --pattern "codefly_*.sbom.json" \
            --pattern checksums.txt

      - name: Attest released archives
        uses: actions/attest@1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6 # v4
        with:
          subject-checksums: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets/checksums.txt

      - name: Attest published SBOMs
        uses: actions/attest@1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6 # v4
        with:
          subject-path: "${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets/*.sbom.json"

  verify:
    name: Verify published release
    needs: attest
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Check out the tagged source
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5

      - name: Verify the published release
        env:
          # Verification reads this repository only and must not depend on the
          # cross-repository publication credential.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="${RELEASE_TAG#v}"
          release_json="$(
            gh api \
              -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10" \
              "repos/codefly-dev/cli/releases/tags/$RELEASE_TAG"
          )"
          test "$(jq -r .immutable <<<"$release_json")" = "true"
          test "$(gh api "repos/codefly-dev/cli/commits/$RELEASE_TAG" --jq .sha)" = "$GITHUB_SHA"

          openssl x509 -in pkg/cliupdate/release-signing-cert.pem -pubkey -noout > "$RUNNER_TEMP/codefly-release-public-key.pem"

          for target in darwin_amd64 darwin_arm64 linux_amd64 linux_arm64; do
            archive="codefly_${version}_${target}.tar.gz"
            sbom="${archive}.sbom.json"
            jq -e --arg name "$archive" '[.assets[].name] | index($name) != null' <<<"$release_json"
            jq -e --arg name "$sbom" '[.assets[].name] | index($name) != null' <<<"$release_json"
          done
          for name in checksums.txt checksums.txt.sig; do
            jq -e --arg name "$name" '[.assets[].name] | index($name) != null' <<<"$release_json"
          done

          verify_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
          gh release download "$RELEASE_TAG" \
            --repo codefly-dev/cli \
            --dir "$verify_dir" \
            --pattern "codefly_${version}_*.tar.gz" \
            --pattern "codefly_${version}_*.sbom.json" \
            --pattern checksums.txt \
            --pattern checksums.txt.sig
          openssl dgst -sha256 \
            -verify "$RUNNER_TEMP/codefly-release-public-key.pem" \
            -signature "$verify_dir/checksums.txt.sig" \
            "$verify_dir/checksums.txt"
          (cd "$verify_dir" && sha256sum --check checksums.txt)
          for artifact in \
            "$verify_dir"/codefly_"${version}"_*.tar.gz \
            "$verify_dir"/codefly_"${version}"_*.sbom.json; do
            gh attestation verify "$artifact" --repo codefly-dev/cli
          done

          RELEASE_PRERELEASE="$(jq -r .prerelease <<<"$release_json")" \
            RELEASE_TAG="$RELEASE_TAG" \
            sh .github/scripts/verify-homebrew-cask.sh
